description: The CO2 warning raised by the sensor monitor from the 2014 replay. The evidence is the place, never a person's exposure. Illustrative only: not seed data.

value.title: CO2 above the habitat limit
value.what: The one-hour average CO2 is 3.5 mmHg. The habitat limit is 3 mmHg.
value.why: High CO2 can cause headaches, shortness of breath and tiredness, and can disturb sleep. It is a limit for the cabin air, not a diagnosis.
steps: Tell the crew and the ground.
The flight control team finds and repairs the CO2 scrubbers or switches on extra scrubbing.

evidence.summary: One-hour mean 3.5 mmHg (4,606 ppm at an assumed 760 mmHg), replayed from 7 Oct 2014. Another mission's cabin, not anyone's exposure.

citation.text: CO2 sensor, Replay of ISS cabin data, 7 Oct 2014. Limit: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 2, Revision F (EV01).
